anchors.statement: Total nonfarm payroll employment fell by 23,000 in July 2026.
anchors.usage_boundary: Single-month estimate is not statistically different from zero at BLS's 90 percent threshold; use with corroboration.

anchors.statement: The unemployment rate was 4.1 percent in July.
anchors.usage_boundary: CPS estimate; changed little over the year.

anchors.statement: May and June payrolls combined were 103,000 lower than previously reported.
anchors.usage_boundary: Use to show that the August 7 information shock included history.

anchors.statement: Hires were 5.348 million with a 3.4 percent rate in June.
anchors.usage_boundary: Below the February 2020 hire rate of 3.9 percent.

anchors.statement: Quits were 3.232 million with a 2.0 percent rate in June.
anchors.usage_boundary: Below the February 2020 quit rate of 2.3 percent.

anchors.statement: Layoffs and discharges were 1.766 million with a 1.1 percent rate in June.
anchors.usage_boundary: Below the February 2020 rate of 1.3 percent.

anchors.statement: Initial unemployment-insurance claims were 209,000 in the week ended August 8, versus 224,000 in the comparable 2025 week.
anchors.source_ref: U.S. Department of Labor weekly claims 2026-08-13 / https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf
anchors.usage_boundary: Strong check against a broad layoff wave; excludes ineligible and nonfiling job losers.

permitted_analysis.statement: The labor market looks frozen without yet breaking.
permitted_analysis.boundary: Capital Chronicle accepted qualitative synthesis; not a recession call or forecast.

permitted_analysis.statement: Weak mobility may be a larger immediate worker risk than mass layoffs.
permitted_analysis.boundary: Capital Chronicle accepted conditional analysis; must remain may-language.

permitted_analysis.statement: A low-motion labor market has less capacity to absorb the next shock without unemployment changing quickly.
permitted_analysis.boundary: Capital Chronicle accepted conditional inference; not a forecast.
